ctx.x: Well that happened because of Roy Eldridge, in Scott Hamilton’s case. Scott preceded me into New York by about six months. He immediately had a gig at Michael’s Pub with Hank Jones, Milt Hinton, himself, and I can’t remember who the drummer was, it was somebody great. You know I can’t even remember, it may have been Jo Jones or somebody, or Connie Kay or one of those.

Grady, possibly Grady. I can’t remember who the drummer was, forgive me whoever it was, but so they warmed up to Scott immediately there, because he’s playing music from their era and nobody has done this, everybody is going [scats] for twenty-five years before that. You know going one-four [scats]. These are my ways of making the over- academicized music sort of to turn it into an onomatopoeia if you will. See I can do it too, academia.
